won_reason: Multi-threaded relationships built across 3 stakeholders — when champion went on leave, deal did not stall

calls.notes: Siddharth is the champion — strong use case for HR analytics. In Call 1 we proactively asked: besides you, who else will use this and who has budget authority? He named Amanda Torres (CHRO) and Dev Kapoor (Finance BP). We scheduled separate introductory calls with both immediately.

Separate call with Amanda Torres. She cares about employee retention data and board reporting. We tailored our pitch entirely to her priorities — not features, but outcomes. She was impressed. Separately called Dev Kapoor and walked him through ROI model. Both are now independently warm.

Siddharth went on medical leave unexpectedly — 3 weeks. In past this would have killed the deal. But Amanda and Dev are both already engaged. Amanda asked us to continue working with her directly. Deal did not miss a beat.

Full group call — Amanda, Dev, and Siddharth back from leave. We presented a combined stakeholder summary showing how the product addresses each person's specific goal. Workday Analytics was mentioned — we had already prepared a comparison doc. Amanda asked about implementation support.

WON. Amanda signed off. She told us that the fact we had relationships with all 3 stakeholders — not just Siddharth — made them feel we were a long-term partner, not just a salesperson. Annual contract with expansion clause signed.

lessons_learned: Multi-thread from Call 1 — always ask who else is involved and meet them separately
Single-threaded deals die when the champion goes absent — build redundancy
Each stakeholder needs their own tailored value story, not the same pitch
When champion goes on leave, multi-threading is what saves the deal
Expansion clause in contract is easier to get when trust is high post strong sales process
